title: I am a steamer fanatic who mostly cooks everything with steam. This is my 12th steamer and is somewhat disappointing.
text:
I am a steamer fanatic who mostly cooks everything with steam. This is my 12th steamer and is somewhat disappointing.. [[VIDEOID:d686991dc4eaf4730ba34a52dbe64089]] I have been steaming most of my meals for over 25 years. In those 25 years, I owned or previously owned 11 steamers. This is my 12th steamer and is somewhat disappointing due to its unusual design and noise.

WHAT is in the BOX
In addition to the instruction manual and one-year limited product warranty pamphlet, this comes in nine parts as follows:
- Power cord
- Two steaming baskets with lid (four items)
- Steaming grate
- Drip tray
- Base unit
- Top lid

FEATURES
- There are two independent steaming controls with ability to synchronize finish or ability to run as a combined steam zone.
- The rapid start feature supposedly reaches max steaming power in less than 30 seconds; however, I did not see steam come out of the vent covers until I was 14 minutes into a 25-minute cycle
- There are two steaming levels (high and low), a keep warm only feature (for 45 minutes), a steaming only feature, or a keep warm (for 15 minutes) after steaming feature.
- It has a descaling option (which I have not tested yet) based on water hardness level, which the user has to test before first use. The water hardness test strip was not included with my unit as specified. I contacted Breville and they said they would send me one. However, it has been a week and they still have not sent it out. I decided to leave the level set to five so that I could use the steamer now.
- Everything but the base and drip tray are metal.
- The unit is easy to operate once one gets the hang of it.

LIKES in order of importance to me
- I love the option of using only the steaming tray because there is more surface area for cooking large items like filets of fish.
- I can split the steamer into two zones with or without a synchronized finish or cook on one side in split-zone mode.
- I can fill the reservoir from the outside as is typical of most but not all steamers.
- There is 45-minute keep warm feature to keep food warm. This is the "keep warm only" feature and can be used to keep food warm that was cooked elsewhere.
- There are no plastic parts exposed to the food. The plastic drip tray sits underneath the steaming tray and sits below the metal steaming basket.
- A full reservoir provides enough steam for at least 45 minutes of steaming.
- Cord has a finger hole for easy removal from socket.
- It beeps when done.
- There are descaling instructions inside the lid.
- The footprint is large and oval, yet sleek looking. It reminds me of a railroad car.

DISLIKES in order of importance to me
- This unit cooks unevenly. During a combined steam, the right side does not steam as well as the left.
- The steamer takes a long time to get up to a good heat level during a cold start (which is most of the time).
- Two steamer baskets are required to make a dozen hard boiled eggs because the main tray does not have egg indentations. This is a MAJOR oversight in my opinion. This means there is more clean-up required (due to being required to use the steamer baskets) and fewer eggs can be hard boiled. If they used an offset method, most likely they could have gotten 18 to 24 egg indentations on the main tray. Each steamer basket has only six indentations per basket.
- Max water level causes water to overflow onto counter. When filling the reservoir to the max level prior to adding the drip tray, it will cause the insertion of the drip tray to displace the water in the tank and overflow on the counter. It is best to fill the tank through the spout; however, avoid filling it to the max level because it overflows. I found the water must always be slightly below the max level. I would have liked a deeper reservoir so that I can fill it to the max fill line; either that or change the max fill line level indicator.
- Operational noise is annoying as it sounds like the unit is grunting.
- The drip tray fills up quickly when steaming some items like potatoes or chicken. Just the act of steaming causes condensation and water to build up. This is typical, so I would have liked a little deeper drip tray. In addition, it is a bit difficult to unseat the tray, so be careful when emptying its hot liquid.
- There are so many moving parts to wash or at least dry (depending on whether food has come in contact with the trays).
- Steam comes out of both sides of the vent cover even when cooking in one of the two split zones and not the other.
- The steamer is heavy.
- No rice bowl is included, although I can use any microwave safe dish.

In summary, I am a bit disappointed in this steamer and give it 2.6 stars (round up to 3 stars). My main disappointment is that it cooks unevenly and takes about 14 minutes to reach peak steam level from a cold start. The right side never steams as well as the left whether in combined or split zone. I dislike how water easily spills onto the counter due to the shallow reservoir and the misleading max fill line. The lack of egg indentations in the steam tray is also a negative for me. The steamer does offer the versatility of cooking two meals at once. Also, plastic is not exposed to the food. However, even if this steamer were fully functional and better designed, it is still overkill for most people. Most people want to cook one item like rice or vegetables. There is just so much to wash and I wash everything by hand. If this steamer did not have the first six negatives, then I would have loved it as a third-place choice for my purpose even though it is smaller than my Richard Simmons three-meal steamer I listed below. In its current functional condition, this steamer is priced too high. If it were better designed, then I would consider the current $165 price reasonable.

Attached are pictures of the steamer on maximum water level and the water almost reaching the spout. Once the drip tray is put in place, the water flows out onto the counter (notice water to top of spout). In the picture where I have two bowls, I was using the split steam zone to cook rolled oatmeal on the left and oat groats on the right. Since the steamer does not cook as well on the right side even though all the settings were correct, I actually had to cook it twice. In the pictures where you see just the steaming tray and potatoes or garlic, I was using the combined zone. Also attached is a video that demonstrates the Breville's noisy “grunts” during use.

For those who are interested, here are MY STEAMERS - PAST and PRESENT

PAST 3 STEAMERS that eventually broke:
--> One small round Black and Decker Steamer (extinct now) which was great and super small but only lasted about two years. This was my first steamer; I purchased it in the mid-1990's.
--> One [[ASIN:B00004SPEI Krups Optisteam Plus]]. I had this since February 1999 and it was my most used steamer and very similar to the Oster steamer.
--> One [[ASIN:B00073HLMU Oster 5711 Mechanical Food Steamer]], which I used daily for my oatmeal and most dinners.

CURRENT 9 STEAMERS:

--> This [[ASIN:B01MZF7ZFZ Breville "Steam Zone" steamer]] which is somewhat disappointing.
--> One [[ASIN:B008FX6KH6 T-fal VC133851 Balanced Living Compact Electric Food Steamer, 4-Quart, Silver]] – this one is too small, is outrageously overpriced, and its steam is not hot enough requiring longer cooking times. I use this one occasionally for rolled oats or some vegetables.
--> One [[ASIN:B00019G8IS Oster 5712 Electronic Food Steamer]] - I use this daily for my oatmeal and most dinners. This is my GOTO steamer.
--> Three [[ASIN:B000JJMER4 Richard Simmons EST7 Steam-Heat Electronic Food Steamers]] which I absolutely love. These are very large steamers and are equivalent to this Breville. This steamer is larger than the Breville (it has three steaming chambers) and good for steaming full meals (protein, starch, and vegetable). This is my second GOTO steamer. This is the type of steamer that is not for everyone and which is why it was discontinued due to lack of customer interest. Because I love it so much, I purchase three as I cannot bear to be without one even though I use the Oster more than this one.
--> One rice steamer, the [[ASIN:B00007J5U7 Zojirushi NS-ZCC10 5-1/2-Cup Neuro Fuzzy Rice Cooker and Warmer, Premium White]], which is excellent but which I do not use nearly enough. It is also a little different that these other steamers in function so they really cannot be compared.
--> One [[ASIN:B003NTXFVG 14" Hard Anodized Non-Stick Wok with Steamer and Lid]]. In addition to this, I also have another very small pot with a steamer on top but I am not counting this one.
--> One Stove-top fish steamer similar to the [[ASIN:B0002IBJG4 Norpro Stainless Steel Fish Poacher]].

description: How do you steam the extra small and the extra large, faster, purer, and with less flavor contamination? With a powerful steamer designed to cook food in the highly efficient steam zone for quickest heat transfer. Use the 16" cooking tray to steam large ingredients like whole fish, or the 7" steaming baskets with independent cooking zones so different ingredients are ready together. Combines the purity of BPA-free parts and all stainless steel cooking surfaces. Powerful 1800W and rapid start ensure your food is cooked evenly and quickly. The smarter, cleaner, faster way to cook.
